findings.Quote: which told her — the way it had told Teo weeks before — that she'd been expected

findings.Fix: cut the Teo aside and let the door's timing speak for itself, or show a concrete detail (Dagny's posture, the room behind her) that proves anticipation

findings.Quote: I won't make you stand in your own doorway while I say more, unless you want me to.
findings.Note: slightly overwritten/self-aware line for the moment, verges on cute meta-commentary about the scene's own staging rather than natural dialogue
findings.Fix: simplify to something more direct, e.g. "That's all, unless you want more."

findings.Quote: she'd rather you understood something first, though, before you spend it on the wrong reason.
findings.Note: slightly abstract/clunky phrasing ('spend it on the wrong reason') for dialogue that's otherwise plain-spoken
findings.Fix: tighten to something like 'before you thank me for the wrong reason'

findings.Quote: Prita asks
findings.Note: tense shift to present tense breaks the past-tense narration used elsewhere in the beat
findings.Fix: change to 'Prita asked'

findings.Quote: That made the thanking harder, not easier.
findings.Note: borders on telling-not-showing the emotional complexity rather than dramatizing it, slightly aphoristic in cadence
findings.Fix: show the hesitation physically or in specific thought rather than summarizing the effect

findings.Quote: the way a person steadies against a weight only she can feel
findings.Fix: cut the abstraction or replace with a concrete physical detail specific to Dagny.

findings.Quote: Prita felt her own throat go tight
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific, less reflexive somatic detail.

findings.Quote: It stayed with her the rest of the day, unfinished.
findings.Note: tells the emotional aftermath rather than showing it, a flat closing summary.
findings.Fix: cut, or ground it in a concrete moment where the question resurfaces.

findings.Quote: the one Sigrun had read aloud twice now
findings.Note: specific detail feels like filler emphasis rather than adding information — reads as padding to justify the day count
findings.Fix: cut to 'Ashgrave's relocation window started counting from the morning after the tally.'

findings.Quote: Forty-one rows. She'd built plenty of documents this year with forty-one rows in them. This was the first one that ended instead of continuing.
findings.Note: the aphoristic contrast ('ended instead of continuing') tips into telling-the-theme rather than showing it; slightly pat given the rest of the passage's dry, procedural register
findings.Fix: trim to let the row count and column list carry the weight without the explicit thematic gloss, e.g. cut the final sentence or make it more concrete (what continuing meant, what ending means in practical terms)

findings.Quote: the frame didn't know an offer had been accepted and wouldn't have cared if it did
findings.Note: borders on a stock personification-of-indifference beat; slightly redundant restating of the same idea twice ('didn't know' / 'wouldn't have cared')
findings.Fix: cut to 'because the frame didn't know an offer had been accepted.'

findings.Quote: Teo entered that line the way she entered every other line, without comment.
findings.Note: Vague abstraction standing in for concrete action; tells us her demeanor without showing anything specific.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete detail of the entry itself.

findings.Quote: because the ledger's job was completeness, not comfort
findings.Note: Aphoristic explainer that tells the reader the theme instead of trusting the preceding image.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause; let the omission speak for itself.

findings.Quote: and hers had never mattered to anyone but her
findings.Note: Slides into a flat statement of emotional significance rather than dramatizing it, a mild telling-not-showing.
findings.Fix: Anchor the claim in a specific detail (e.g., who never asked, what she never said) rather than a general assertion.

findings.Quote: It didn't take long. It was never going to take long.
findings.Fix: cut the redundant second sentence or replace with a concrete detail

findings.Quote: because there was nowhere else the evening had ever been going to end
findings.Note: Vague fatalistic filler asserting inevitability without earning it in-scene; tells rather than shows why the shop is the only destination.
findings.Fix: Cut the abstraction and give a concrete reason he goes down, e.g. naming what's waiting on the bench.

findings.Quote: the way a person stops noticing his own house
findings.Note: Generic explanatory simile that states a universal truth instead of sharpening the specific sensory image already built.
findings.Fix: Drop the simile and let the preceding sensory list carry the point.

findings.Quote: habit more than inspection, though tonight he was doing both at once without quite meaning to
findings.Note: slightly over-explains an already-clear beat, telling us the nuance rather than trusting the gesture
findings.Fix: cut the trailing clause or shorten to 'though tonight it was inspection too'

findings.Quote: Keeping faith with something. That was closer.
findings.Note: the correction-of-word-choice move risks reading as a reached-for aphorism rather than earned realization
findings.Fix: ground it in a concrete detail instead, e.g. tie 'keeping faith' to a specific act he still performs

findings.Quote: tracing them slowly enough that a watcher might have mistaken it for grief
findings.Note: Hedges the emotion by attributing it to a hypothetical watcher rather than committing to what the character feels; slightly evasive telling-not-showing.
findings.Fix: Cut the hedge; show the gesture and let grief be inferred without narrating how it might be misread.

findings.Quote: Arguing with a tag was even less use than arguing with a jig, and he'd learned that lesson from the other side of it.
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler comparison that doesn't clarify the situation and reads as a stock wisdom-quip.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile or replace with a concrete detail about what arguing with a jig once cost him.

findings.Quote: a thing many times and expect to do it many more
findings.Note: vague filler phrasing that tells rather than shows competence/routine
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete detail of their practiced motion

findings.Quote: a ground it hadn't touched since before it was built
findings.Note: slightly overreaching/vague claim asserted without support, reads as portentous filler
findings.Fix: specify what grounds this claim or trim to something concrete

findings.Quote: taking no more notice of the day than it took of any other Tuesday
findings.Note: Stock personification-of-indifference phrasing that reads as filler wit rather than earned observation.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more concrete, setting-specific comparison or cut.

findings.Quote: gathering along the outer ring the way they gathered for nothing else all year
findings.Note: vague comparative claim that tells rather than shows communal significance without specifics
findings.Fix: name one concrete prior gathering (a festival, a memorial) to ground the comparison

findings.Quote: exactly the way a healthy descent should sound
findings.Note: asserts a technical judgment without grounding it in sensory or character detail, reads as authorial reassurance rather than earned observation
findings.Fix: specify what a healthy descent sounds like (e.g., 'the pitch dropping in even steps, no catch in it') so the claim is demonstrated, not stated
